chunks: And it is narrated from Abū al-Maghrāʾ, who said:

A man asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام while I was with him, and said: “May Allah rectify you. I pass by the official, or I go to the official, and he gives me dirhams as a grant; should I take them?” He said: “Yes.”
I said: “And may I perform hajj with them?” He said: “Yes, and perform hajj with them.”

key_terms.آخُذُهَا: should I take it, referring to accepting the money
key_terms.أَبِي الْمَغْرَاءِ: Abū al-Maghrāʾ, the narrator reporting this hadith
key_terms.أَحُجُّ: I perform hajj, referring to undertaking the pilgrimage
key_terms.الْعَامِلِ: the official or state functionary being referred to
key_terms.بِالدَّرَاهِمِ: in dirhams, meaning monetary payment or grant
key_terms.حُجَّ: perform hajj, an imperative instruction to carry it out

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to accept money from a government official and perform hajj with it?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates the permissibility of accepting dirhams granted by a government official and using them for lawful purposes. It further affirms that one may even perform hajj with such money, indicating its permissibility in this context.
